name: Asura
classification_notes: An uppercase-only display face with sharp stroke ends and irregular skeletons that read closer to hand-lettered signage than a formal script, so it sits in display rather than script proper.
summary: An uppercase-only display face that reads like a 19th-century sign painter reinventing the alphabet after too much coffee.
description: Asura is an early-access display typeface still in progress, currently covering uppercase, digits and basic punctuation in a single weight. Its sharp stroke ends, unpredictable bends and mischievous letterforms borrow the energy of poster-era sign painting rather than any tidy historical model. Bought early, it comes with free updates as Abhijit Menon continues drawing out the lower case and further weights.
foundry_blurb: Described as a feral, free-flowing display typeface that mixes poster-era elegance with a hint of delightful chaos. Its sharp stroke ends, unpredictable bends, and mischievous letter skeletons make it feel like a 19th-century French sign painter had a caffeine rush and decided to reinvent the alphabet.
